response.rationale: R1 is the only candidate that unifies the raw evidence of medullary thyroid carcinoma (calcitonin 10 506 pg/mL, CEA 2750 ng/mL, bilateral calcified thyroid nodules) with pheochromocytoma (episodic palpitations/sweating/headaches, metanephrines >10 000 µg), the classic MEN2 combination. R2 captures only the MTC component and R3 only the catecholamine excess; neither explains the full syndrome. The denied family history is a counterfactual but does not exclude de novo MEN2.

rejected.why: Explains the catecholamine excess and pheochromocytoma symptoms but ignores the markedly elevated calcitonin/CEA and calcified thyroid nodules, so it cannot account for the MTC component.
